headline: Paderborn let a 2-0 lead slip, but the fixture still favours them
summary: Paderborn led 2-0 at Werder Bremen on Saturday and drew 2-2 — that is one win in their last five Bundesliga games. Hamburger SV arrive with three straight wins, though the run has been built on scoring: 13 conceded. The fixture still points to the hosts, who have never lost to Hamburg — three wins, two draws, all in the second tier. Across 6 bookmakers, margin removed, Paderborn are 39.7% to Hamburg's 34.0%, and the handicap is level at 0. Over 3.0 goals is a 49.1% chance.
read: Hamburger SV come in on three straight wins and sit ninth, while Paderborn are 16th with one win in five and were pegged back from 2-0 at Werder Bremen on Saturday. The market still makes the hosts narrow favourites at 39.7% to 34.0% with the handicap level, and sets the 50/50 goal total just under three.

facts.fact: Paderborn are narrow home favourites at 39.7% against HSV's 34.0%, with the handicap set at level (+0).
Hamburger SV have won each of their last three Bundesliga matches, against Köln, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart.
facts.meaning: The visitors arrive as the form side of the two and sit ninth, above the hosts.

facts.fact: Paderborn have taken one win from their last five Bundesliga games (DLWLL).
facts.meaning: A promoted side short of results, and German media describe them as under pressure before this home game.

facts.fact: Paderborn conceded chances worth 3.21 xG in Saturday's 2-2 at Werder Bremen, after leading 2-0.
facts.meaning: They were cut open repeatedly in the game they let slip, and HSV's attack is the next test of that back line.

facts.fact: Hamburger SV have conceded 13 goals across their last five league matches.
facts.meaning: The winning run has been built on scoring, not on solidity — they have shipped five twice this season.

facts.meaning: Three goals is roughly a coin flip — the market expects an open game, not a tight one.

facts.fact: Paderborn are unbeaten in their last five meetings with HSV — three wins and two draws, including 2-0 at home in March 2025.
facts.meaning: The head-to-head is the strongest argument for the hosts, who have handled this opponent repeatedly in the second division.

facts.fact: 29 of Paderborn's 30 senior players trained on Wednesday, with only Oliver Batista Meier absent.
facts.meaning: The hosts have an almost full squad for a home game they are under pressure to take something from.

sources.fact: Paderborn are under pressure going into the match, having drawn 2-2 with Werder Bremen after leading 2-0.
29 of Paderborn's 30 senior squad players trained on Wednesday, with only Oliver Batista Meier absent.
Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant has completed his first full training session with Paderborn in several months as he steps up his comeback.
Paderborn led 2-0 at Werder Bremen but were pegged back to 2-2, a result that highlighted the promoted side's remaining weaknesses.
Rayan Philippe, who celebrates his 26th birthday on Friday, faces his former club HSV on Saturday.
Steffen Tigges made his first Paderborn start in eight months at Bremen and rewarded the choice by scoring.
Hamburger SV are on a three-match winning run, which they aim to extend at Paderborn.
Albert Sambi Lokonga has resumed full training after a muscular problem and is on track to return to the HSV squad against Paderborn, though he may not start immediately.
